feasibility.verdict: Partially feasible: single-column ELM+PFLOTRAN can simulate fertilizer-N cycling and vertical nitrate leaching flux below the root zone, but cannot resolve 3-D lateral groundwater transport to specific wells or true arrival concentrations at well screens.
answerable: Nitrate production/immobilization in the soil N cycle under corn/soybean fertilization
Vertical nitrate leaching flux and pore-water NO3 concentration below the root zone
Seasonal/interannual timing of leaching pulses tied to fertilizer timing and drainage
Sensitivity of leaching to soil texture and fertilizer rate across representative fields
not_answerable: Lateral advective-dispersive transport from field to a specific drinking-water well
Actual arrival concentrations at well screens (requires 3-D saturated-zone groundwater/transport model, e.g., regional PFLOTRAN or MODFLOW-MT3D)
Travel-time distributions and mixing in the aquifer between recharge and well capture zone
Well-specific dilution, denitrification along flow paths in the saturated zone

parsed.n_justification: Four columns capture the dominant land-management and soil-texture gradients driving nitrate leaching in the Upper Iowa basin: two tile-drained corn fields on contrasting silty clay loam vs. loam soils, one corn-soybean rotation field, and one lower-rate/reduced-input field. This spans the leaching source-term variability that feeds any downstream aquifer transport model without over-fitting a single-column setup.
requires_capabilities: ELM active N-cycle (CN/BGC) with prognostic soil mineral N and leaching
Managed crop mode (ELM crop model) with fertilizer application and corn/soybean PFTs
Tile drainage / subsurface drainage representation for lower-flux fields
ELM-PFLOTRAN coupling for vertical variably-saturated reactive nitrate transport in the soil column
External regional 3-D groundwater flow-and-transport model (PFLOTRAN saturated-zone or MODFLOW-MT3D) to translate column leaching fluxes into well arrival concentrations
assumptions: Leaching flux (SMIN_NO3_LEACHED / QDRAI_NO3) at the base of the soil column is used as the source term boundary condition for downstream aquifer transport, not as a well concentration itself
GSWP3 / CLMNCEP atmospheric forcing 1999-2018 is representative of recent climate; first 10 years treated as spin-up plus AD/transient BGC spin-up prior to analysis
Fertilizer rates follow default managed-corn N application (~150-200 kg N/ha) with the reduced-input column scaled to ~60% of that
Nitrogen deposition from default ELM NDEP dataset for the region
Single-column geometry ignores lateral hillslope flow; arrival-concentration estimation is deferred to a coupled 3-D transport step outside single-column ELM
